idea: A small-batch home bakery in Austin
facts: Also wants to sell to cafés

book.name: Sugar & Sage
book.oneLiner: Austin's neighbourhood bakery without the storefront: slow sourdough and made-to-order cakes sold at markets and online.

pitch.problem: Good bread in Austin means a drive across town and a queue.
pitch.solution: A weekly market stall plus online pre-orders, so nothing is baked without a buyer.
pitch.who: Families in South and East Austin who shop the Saturday markets.
pitch.whyNow: Farmers markets in Austin have doubled since 2020.
pitch.howItMakesMoney: Loaves at $9-12, cakes at $85-160, pre-orders paid up front.
pitch.first90Days: Certificates, two markets, 40 loaves a week by week 12.
pitch.risks: Cottage-food sales cap; one oven; seasonality.

money.breakEven: About 55 loaves and 4 cakes a month, roughly two good market Saturdays.

leaner.title: Cakes-only from home
leaner.whatChanges: Skip the market stall and the second oven; sell celebration cakes by pre-order only. You give up walk-up customers but cut start-up costs by half.

assumptions.text: You will bake from your home kitchen, not a rented one.
Occasion cakes are the main earner.
assumptions.because: you said cakes are where the money is

assumptions.text: Your customers are families, not cafés.
assumptions.because: you talked about markets and occasion cakes

assumptions.text: Cottage-food rules apply because you sell direct from home.

names.name: Sugar & Sage
names.why: Sweet and herbal, sounds like a kitchen.

brand.voice: Warm, unfussy, a little playful. Talks like a neighbour, not a brand.

vision.manifesto: Sugar & Sage is the bakery my neighbourhood didn't know it was missing. Every Saturday the loaves sell out by ten.
vision.why: Because my grandmother's kitchen was where everyone gathered, and I want mine to be that too.
vision.dayInTheLife: I'm up at five, the ovens already warm. By eight the car is packed with forty loaves and two cakes wrapped in ribbon. The market regulars queue before the tent is up; a mother picks up a birthday cake and cries a little. I'm home by two, feet up, orders for next week already pinging in.
vision.firstPost: Sugar & Sage is open! Slow-fermented sourdough and celebration cakes, baked in small batches in South Austin. Find us Saturdays at the market or order online. #sugarandsage #austinbakery #sourdough

legal.summary: Because you bake at home and sell directly, Texas treats you as a cottage food operation. No health permit, but labelling rules, a food handler card and a sales cap apply.

structures.name: Sole proprietor
structures.summary: You and the business are the same thing.

items.title: Texas food handler certificate
items.why: Required for every cottage food operator.
items.body: Texas Department of State Health Services

verified.note: Confirmed on dshs.texas.gov; course must be accredited.

items.title: Cottage food rules: labels and sales cap
items.why: No permit needed, but labels must carry set wording.

items.title: Sales and use tax permit
items.why: Needed before your first taxable sale.

items.title: Assumed name certificate (DBA)
items.why: Trade as Sugar & Sage rather than your own name.

items.title: General liability insurance
items.why: Most markets require proof of cover.

funding.name: Bootstrapping from pre-orders
funding.fits: Cakes are paid up front; use deposits to fund ingredients.

needs.why: Card sales roughly double market takings.

options.name: Square
options.note: No monthly fee; pay per tap.

path.target: Realistically 6 to 8 weeks from today, in time for the fall markets.

steps.title: Choose sole proprietor to start
steps.detail: Nothing to file; revisit an LLC once sales are steady.

steps.title: Lock the name: Sugar & Sage
steps.detail: Check the county assumed-name register first.

steps.title: Take the food handler course
steps.detail: Keep the certificate with you at markets.

steps.title: Apply for the sales tax permit
steps.detail: Online; allow up to two weeks.

steps.title: File the assumed name (DBA)
steps.detail: Bring photo ID to the county clerk.

steps.title: Get liability insurance
steps.detail: Markets ask for proof before you can sell.

steps.title: Order the card reader
steps.detail: Square ships in a few days.

steps.title: Apply to two Saturday markets
steps.detail: Attach insurance and food handler certificate.

steps.title: Test-bake the market menu twice
steps.detail: Time the full bake, packing and load-out.

steps.title: Ta-da: Sugar & Sage exists
steps.detail: First market Saturday, first loaf sold.
